The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save.
description: Yellow mold grows in dark places, and one patch covers a 5-foot square.

name: Crossbow Trap
trigger: A creature that walks through the trip wire triggers the trap.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the trip wire.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disables the trip wire, and a check with a total of 5 or lower triggers the trap.

effect: The trap makes two attacks against the triggering creature. Each attack has a +8 attack bonus and deals 5 (1d10) piercing damage on a hit. This attack can't gain advantage or disadvantage.
description: The crossbow trap is a favorite of kobolds and other creatures that rely on traps to defend their lairs. It consists of a trip wire strung across a hallway and connected to a pair of hidden heavy crossbows. The crossbows are aimed to fire down the hallway at anyone who disturbs the trip wire.

name: Falling Portcullis
trigger: A creature that steps on the pressure plate triggers the trap.

detection.detail: A successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the pressure plate.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disables it, and a check with a total of 5 or lower triggers the trap.

effect: An iron portcullis drops from the ceiling, blocking an exit or a passageway.
description: Some folk who build dungeons, such as mad wizards in search of new victims, have no intention of allowing their visitors to make an easy escape. A falling portcullis trap can be especially devious if it causes a portcullis to drop some distance away from the pressure plate that activates the trap. Although the trap is deep in the dungeon, the portcullis closes off the dungeon entrance, which is hundreds of feet away, meaning that adventurers don't know they are trapped until they decide to head for the exit.

name: Fiery Blast
trigger: Anyone who steps on the mosaic causes fire to erupt from it. Those who openly wear holy symbols of Pyremius don't trigger this trap.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the presence of ash and faint burn marks in the area affected by this trap.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Religion) check enables a creature to destroy the trap by defacing a key rune on the perimeter of the mosaic that is within reach; failing this check causes the trap to activate. A successful dispel magic (DC 15) cast on the runes destroys the trap.

effect: A 15-foot cube of fire erupts, covering the pressure plate and the area around it. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 24 (7d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: The temple of Pyremius, a god of fire, is threatened by thieves who seek to steal the fire opals displayed there by the priests in tribute to their god. A mosaic on the floor of the entryway to the inner sanctum delivers a fiery rebuke to intruders.

name: Net Trap
trigger: A trip wire strung across a hallway is rigged to a large net. If the trip wire is broken, the net falls on intruders. An iron bell is also rigged to the trip wire. It rings when the trap activates, alerting nearby guards.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the trip wire and the net.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disables the trip wire without causing the net to drop or the bell to ring; failing the check causes the trap to activate.

effect: A net covering a 10-foot-by-10-foot area centered on the trip wire falls to the floor as a bell rings. Any creature fully within this area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be restrained. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check to try to free itself or another creature in the net. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10, 20 hp) also frees a creature without harming the creature.
area: 10-foot-by-10-foot area centered on the trip wire
description: A trip wire rigged to a large net and an iron bell, used by goblins to capture intruders alive.

name: Pit Trap
trigger: Anyone who steps on the canvas might fall into the pit.

detection.detail: A successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the presence of the canvas and the 1-foot-wide ledge around the edges of the pit where it is safe to travel.

effect: The triggering creature must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. On a successful save, the creature catches itself on the pit's edge or instinctively steps back. On a failed save, the creature falls into the pit and takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage from the fall.
description: A simple pit trap consisting of a 10-foot-deep hole concealed by tattered canvas covered with leaves and dirt.

name: Scything Blade
trigger: When the lever is pulled, the trap activates.

detection.detail: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check involving the surfaces in the trap's area of effect reveals scrape marks and bloodstains on the walls and floor.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 15 Dexterity check using thieves' tools disables the lever.

effect: Each Medium or larger creature in a 5-foot-wide, 20-foot-long area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A trap using moving blades that sweep down through a chamber, activated by a lever.

name: Sleep of Ages
trigger: Stepping on the pressure plate triggers this trap.

detection.detail: A successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check reveals the pressure plate.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check made within 5 feet of the pressure plate disables the trap, and a check with a total of 10 or lower triggers it. A successful dispel magic (DC 19) cast on the pressure plate destroys the trap.

effect: When activated, this trap casts a sleep spell centered on the pressure plate, using a 9th-level spell slot.
description: A pressure plate that unleashes a sleep spell when activated.

name: Path of Blades
trigger: The trap activates based on initiative count 10. Active Elements: The Path of Blades includes a set of whirling blades along the first 80 feet of the trap, crushing pillars that slam down from the ceiling to the floor before rising back up to the ceiling in the next 50 feet, and a rune of fear in its final 30 feet.

detection.detail: Intelligence (Investigation), DC 15. As an action, a creature that can see the blades can attempt an Intelligence (Investigation) check. A successful check means that the character has learned how to anticipate the blades' movement, imposing disadvantage on the blades' attacks against the creature while it isn't incapacitated.

disarm.detail: Dexterity check using thieves' tools, DC 15. Creatures can use thieves' tools in the area attacked by the blades to foil their mechanism. A successful check reduces the Whirling Blades attack bonus by 2. The blades are disabled if their attack bonus is reduced to -8. Rune of Fear: The rune can be disabled with three successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) checks. Each check requires an action. A creature must be at the end of the hallway to attempt the check, and only one creature can work on this task at once. Once a creature attempts a check for this purpose, no other character can do so until the end of that creature's next turn. Alternatively, the rune can be disabled with three successful castings of dispel magic (DC 13) targeting the rune.

effect: Whirling Blades (Initiative 20). The blades attack each creature in the first 80 feet of the hallway, with a +5 bonus to the attack roll and dealing 11 (2d10) slashing damage on a hit. Crushing Pillars (Initiative 10). Each creature in the 50-foot-long area beyond the first 80 feet of the hallway must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone. Rune of Fear (Initiative 10). Each creature in the 30-foot-long area beyond the Crushing Pillars must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature becomes frightened by the rune, and it must immediately use its reaction to move its speed in the direction of the pillars. The frightened creature can't move closer to the far end of the hallway until it uses its action to make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw, which ends the frightened condition on itself on a success. Dynamic Elements. The blades and the rune become more dangerous the longer the trap remains active. Blades Accelerate. The blades move with increasing speed, slowing only when they hit a target. Each time the blades miss with an attack, their next attack becomes harder to avoid. After each miss, the blades' attack bonus increases by 2, and their damage increases by 3 (1d6). These benefits apply until the blades hit a target, after which the values return to normal. Rune's Defense. Tampering with the Rune of Fear increases the trap's power. Each successful check on an attempt to disable the rune increases the damage of the blades and the crushing pillars by 5 (1d10) and increases the rune's saving throw DC by 1. Constant Elements. The Whirling Blades and the Rune of Fear affect each creature that ends its turn in an area affected by these elements. Whirling Blades. Any creature that ends its turn in the blades' area is targeted by an attack: +5 attack bonus; 5 (1d10) slashing damage on a hit. Rune of Fear. Any creature that ends its turn within 30 feet of the far end of the corridor must make a saving throw against the Rune of Fear effect. Countermeasures. Each of the trap's active elements can be thwarted by particular countermeasures. Whirling Blades. Characters can smash the blades, damage their components, or discern how to avoid them. The blades are disabled if their attack bonus is reduced to -8. Ways to reduce it are described below. Intelligence (Investigation), DC 15. As an action, a creature that can see the blades can attempt an Intelligence (Investigation) check. A successful check means that the character has learned how to anticipate the blades' movement, imposing disadvantage on the blades' attacks against the creature while it isn't incapacitated. Attack. A creature in the area can ready an attack to strike at one of the blades as it goes by. The blade gains advantage on its attack against the creature. The creature then attacks. Each blade has AC 15 and 15 hit points. Destroying a blade reduces the Whirling Blades attack bonus by 2. Dexterity check using thieves' tools, DC 15. Creatures can use thieves' tools in the area attacked by the blades to foil their mechanism. A successful check reduces the Whirling Blades attack bonus by 2. Crushing Pillars. The pillars are not susceptible to countermeasures. Rune of Fear. The rune can be disabled with three successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) checks. Each check requires an action. A creature must be at the end of the hallway to attempt the check, and only one creature can work on this task at once. Once a creature attempts a check for this purpose, no other character can do so until the end of that creature's next turn. Alternatively, the rune can be disabled with three successful castings of dispel magic (DC 13) targeting the rune.
area: The trap occupies a hallway: first 80 feet (whirling blades), next 50 feet (crushing pillars), final 30 feet (rune of fear).
description: The Path of Blades includes a set of whirling blades along the first 80 feet of the trap, crushing pillars that slam down from the ceiling to the floor before rising back up to the ceiling in the next 50 feet, and a rune of fear in its final 30 feet.

name: Sphere of Crushing Doom
trigger: This trap activates as soon as the door leading to the jester's coffin is opened. A magic portal opens at the northern end of the hallway and disgorges an enormous steel sphere, which hurtles down the slope. When it reaches the bottom of the slope, a second portal briefly appears and teleports the sphere back to the top of the slope to begin the process again.

detection.detail: No detection method specified in the source text.

disarm.detail: Either portal can be neutralized with three successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) checks, but the process of analyzing a portal to disrupt it takes time. Faint runes in the ceiling and floor at both ends of the hallway are involved in the functioning of the portals. A creature must first use an action to examine a set of runes, then use a subsequent action to attempt to vandalize the runes. Each successful check reduces the sphere's damage by 11 (2d10), as the disrupted sphere loses speed moving through the failing portal. Alternatively, a set of runes can be disabled with three successful castings of dispel magic (DC 19) targeting any of the runes in the set. If the southern portal is destroyed, the sphere slams into the south wall and comes to a halt. It blocks the door to the tomb, but the characters can escape.

effect: The trap's active element is a sphere of steel that almost fills the 10-foot width of the hallway and rolls to the bottom of the slope on its turn. Each creature in the sphere's path must make a DC 20 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone. Objects that block the sphere, such as a conjured wall, take maximum damage from the impact. After its turn, the sphere gains speed, represented by its damage increasing by 11 (2d10). While its damage is 55 (10d10) or greater, it acts on initiative count 20 and 10.
area: 10-foot width of the hallway, along the slope
description: A complex trap that rolls an enormous steel sphere down a sloped hallway, teleporting it back to the top via portals to repeat the process, growing more lethal each round.

name: Poisoned Tempest
trigger: This trap activates when a ruby is pried from one of the statues. Each statue's mouth slides open, revealing a 1-foot-wide pipe that runs down its throat.

detection.detail: To open the doors, a character must first succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check to find the locking mechanism.

disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check is required to disable the sphere of force that surrounds the lock (dispel magic is ineffective against it). Success on a DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves' tools picks the lock. Finally, a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check is needed to push the door open. Each check requires an action.

effect: The trap fills the room with poison and other deadly effects. Locked Doors (Initiative 20): The four doors to this room slam shut and are locked in place by magic. This effect activates only once, the first time the trap is triggered. Poison Gas (Initiative 20): Poison gas floods the room. Each creature inside must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw, taking 33 (6d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Tempest (Initiative 10): Air and gas boils from the trap. Roll a d6: 1 - Hallucinatory gas scrambles the mind and senses. All Intelligence and Wisdom checks made in the room have disadvantage until the Tempest element activates again. 2 - Explosive gas fills the area. If anyone holds an open flame, it causes an explosion. All creatures in the area must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The flame is then extinguished. 3 - Weakening gas fills the room. All Strength and Dexterity checks made in the room have disadvantage until the Tempest element activates again. 4 - Buffeting winds force each creature in the room to succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. 5 - Smoke fills the room. Visibility is reduced to 1 foot until the next time the Tempest element activates. 6 - Poison floods the room, forcing creatures to make saving throws as for the Poison Gas element. Increased Potency: The damage from the Poison Gas element increases by 11 (2d10) each round after it activates, to a maximum of 55 (10d10).
description: A fiendish complex trap built to eliminate intruders in a yuan-ti temple, filling a room with poison gas and other deadly effects when a ruby is pried from one of four serpent statues.

name: Sphere of Force Lock Trap
trigger: A character attempts to open the locked door.

detection.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check to find the locking mechanism.

disarm.method: Intelligence (Arcana) check to disable the sphere of force, then Dexterity check using thieves' tools to pick the lock, then Strength (Athletics) check to push the door open.
disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check is required to disable the sphere of force that surrounds the lock (dispel magic is ineffective against it). Success on a DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves' tools picks the lock. Finally, a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check is needed to push the door open. Each check requires an action.

effect: The door is locked and surrounded by a sphere of force. Disabling the sphere and picking the lock allows the door to be opened with a Strength check.
area: The locked door and its surrounding area.
description: A locked door protected by a sphere of force that must be disabled before the lock can be picked and the door forced open.

name: Poison Gas Statues Trap
trigger: The trap activates when characters enter the area, causing statues to emit poison gas.

detection.detail: Not specified in the provided text.

disarm.method: Dexterity check using thieves' tools or Strength check to block the statue, or Strength check to break it (which increases damage).
disarm.detail: A successful DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves' tools, or a successful DC 15 Strength check made to block up the statue with a cloak or similar object, decreases the poison damage by 5 (1d10). Once a character succeeds on the check, someone must remain next to the statue to keep it blocked up. When all four statues are blocked in this manner, the trap deactivates. Reducing a statue to 0 hit points (AC 17; 20 hp; resistance to fire, piercing, and slashing damage; immune to poison and psychic damage) or making a successful DC 20 Strength check to break it cracks the statue and increases the Poison Gas damage by 5 (1d10).

effect: The statues emit poison gas, dealing damage each round. Blocking a statue reduces damage by 5 (1d10); breaking a statue increases damage by 5 (1d10). When all four statues are blocked, the trap deactivates.
damage: Poison Gas damage (base not specified, modified by ±5 (1d10) per statue)
area: The area around the four statues.
description: Four statues emit poison gas; blocking them reduces damage, breaking them increases it, and blocking all four deactivates the trap.

name: Covered Pit
trigger: A creature steps onto the false floor covering the pit.

detection.detail: Spot the false floor, possibly concealed by a sprinkling of dirt or gravel.

disarm.detail: Disable or secure the false floor.

effect: The false floor gives way, dropping the creature into the pit. The pit might be empty, filled with mud (causing anything trapped in it to eventually drown), or have spikes at the bottom.
description: Simple yet effective, a covered pit trap is a hole covered with a false floor and perhaps concealed by a sprinkling of dirt or gravel.

name: Door Trap
trigger: A creature opens or interacts with the trapped door.

detection.detail: Spot the trap on the door.

disarm.detail: Disable the trap mechanism.

effect: The trap triggers, affecting the creature that triggered it or those nearby.
description: In a seldom-used cavern with a high ceiling, a beholder might erect a wall that doesn't reach the ceiling and build a trapped door into it. The beholder can fly over the trap, while intruders are forced to deal with the door or waste time trying to climb over the wall.

name: Glyph Trap on Door
trigger: Triggered when characters open or touch the door to Palish's laboratory.

detection.detail: Not specified in the text.

disarm.detail: Not specified in the text.

effect: If characters trigger the glyph trap on the door, Palish grabs her gear and heads out through a secret door in the back of her living quarters as quickly as possible, closing the door behind her.
description: A glyph trap is placed on the door to Palish's laboratory. Triggering it alerts Palish, who then escapes through a secret door.

name: Weakened Staircase
trigger: A creature that weighs more than 100 pounds steps on the fragile board located 10 feet off the ground.

detection.detail: Can be spotted by anyone on the stairs who has a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 13 or higher.

disarm.detail: The gap that the collapsing board creates can be easily avoided by other creatures walking up the stairs.

effect: The board collapses and the creature falls 10 feet to the ground below.
area: One step of the catwalk staircase
description: One of the steps of the catwalk staircase is ready to collapse.

name: Puzzle Floor
trigger: If an individual applies more than a few pounds of pressure to any square except the one corresponding to the lit-up square on the door, magical flames blast out from the walls.

detection.detail: Even if someone can see that area of the door, the glow is so faint that a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check is needed to notice it.

disarm.detail: This trigger and trap are magical, so they can't be disarmed or jammed mechanically. Casting dispel magic on the floor tiles disables the trap for 1 hour.

effect: Magical flames blast out from the walls. Every creature on the terrace when the flames appear must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: The terrace (16-foot-high terrace with tiled floor)
description: A tiled floor puzzle where stepping on the wrong square triggers magical flames from the walls.

name: Puzzle Door Glyph
trigger: If wrong squares are pressed, the squares are pressed in the wrong order, or they're pressed by the wrong people, a glyph of warding on the door triggers a thunderwave spell.

detection.detail: Finding the glyph requires a thorough search of the door and a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

effect: A glyph of warding on the door triggers a thunderwave spell. Every creature on the ledge when the spell triggers must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 9 (2d8) thunder damage, is pushed 10 feet away from the door, and falls into area 6C, setting off the trap there. A creature that succeeds on the save takes half damage and is not pushed.
description: A glyph of warding on a puzzle door that triggers a thunderwave spell when the wrong squares are pressed.

name: Trapped Steps
trigger: Each of steps 3, 10, 17, and 23 has a glyph of warding spell placed on it, set to trigger when the step is walked on. Creatures emulating Man and Crocodile don't trigger the glyphs.

detection.detail: To spot a glyph, the dust on the step must be cleared away, and a character searching the step must succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

effect: Each triggered glyph releases a 20-foot-radius sphere of lightning centered on the step. Every creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (5d8) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Creatures emulating Man and Crocodile have disadvantage on the saving throw.
description: Glyphs of warding on specific steps of a spiral staircase that release lightning when triggered.

name: Falling Bricks
trigger: If the jug is picked up by anyone else (not emulating Man and Crocodile), loose bricks begin to fall from the ceiling.
effect: Every creature in area 6E is struck by falling bricks and must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that starts its turn in the room repeats the saving throw. After 3 rounds, the bricks stop falling.
description: A trap that causes loose bricks to fall from the ceiling when the alchemy jug is picked up improperly.

name: Concealed Pit
trigger: The first character to step on the pit falls in.

detection.detail: The lead character spots the pit with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

effect: The first character to step on a pit falls in, taking 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage and landing on 1d4 stakes, each of which deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
damage: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning plus 1d4 stakes each dealing 3 (1d6) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison
area: 5 feet wide, 10 feet deep, lined with poisoned wooden stakes
description: A concealed pit 5 feet wide, 10 feet deep, and lined with poisoned wooden stakes.

name: Treasury Lower Lock Trap
trigger: The trap is triggered if an attempt to pick the lower lock fails by 5 or more, if the wrong key is used in the lock, or if it's opened by any means before the upper lock.

detection.detail: The trap can be spotted with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: It's impossible to disarm or bypass.

effect: The trap causes the metal gantry between the treasury and the forge (area 4) to retract west, leaving a 40-foot gap across the magma. The bridge can be re-extended only by lifting the lever in the corridor from area 4. The lever is too far away to be manipulated with mage hand by anyone on the treasury side of the magma river.
area: The metal gantry between the treasury and the forge (area 4)
description: A trap on the lower lock of the treasury door that retracts the gantry across the magma river when triggered.

name: Drugged Fruit and Wine
trigger: A character eats or drinks the drugged fruit or wine.

detection.detail: The contamination can be detected only by someone who has proficiency in Medicine and who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: Characters who eat or drink must make a successful DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour or until they drink 2 quarts of water.
description: A tray of fruit and wine artfully drugged in Zalkore's lair.

name: Dreaming Tincture
trigger: A character drinks a dose of the tincture.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: On a failed save, the character begins to experience illusory sights, sounds, smells, and sensations that seem real. Casting a lesser restoration spell or similar magic on the character ends the effect, which otherwise lasts for 1d4 + 4 hours.
description: A tincture found in Zalkore's lair that causes hallucinations when consumed.

name: Swinging Log Trap
trigger: A character moving through the passage has a 50 percent chance to trip the trigger wire.

detection.detail: can be spotted with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check

effect: Each creature in the passage when the log swings through must make a successful DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 10 (3d6) piercing damage and be knocked prone.
description: A swinging log studded with spikes traps the north passage connecting this chamber to the cart track.

name: Tripwire Alarm
trigger: Approaching enemies trigger a tripwire.

detection.detail: Notice the tripwires with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check; otherwise, they're noticed by anyone with a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 13 or higher.

effect: If approaching enemies are noticed by sentries or trigger a tripwire, the village goes on alert, making it impossible to sneak in.
description: A tripwire alarm that alerts the village when triggered.

name: Village Launch Mechanism
trigger: Cutting the thick vine.

detection.detail: A character who gets a good look at the village in daylight and succeeds on a DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check spots the network of vines and the bent tree and recognizes them as a gigantic spring trap. Those with proficiency in the Survival skill have advantage on this check.

effect: The village is launched. Anyone inside the net when the village is launched and hits the ground must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A gigantic spring trap that launches the village.

name: Poison Gas Trap (Shagambi's Shrine Pedestal)
trigger: Any physical attempt to force open the stone hatch in the top of the pedestal

detection.detail: With a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, a character notices tiny holes in the relief. Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the poison gas from penetrating through when the pedestal is disturbed.

disarm.method: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax
disarm.detail: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the poison gas from penetrating through when the pedestal is disturbed.

effect: A cloud of gas releases through the holes in the wall relief. The gas fills a 15-foot cube directly in front of the mural. Creatures in the area must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) poison damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The gas affects a creature even if it holds its breath or doesn't need to breathe. The gas doesn't linger.
area: 15-foot cube directly in front of the mural
description: A poison gas trap triggered by forcing open the stone hatch on the pedestal in Shagambi's shrine, releasing gas through tiny holes in the wall relief.

name: Covered Pit Trap
trigger: A creature stepping on a pit cover causes it to swing open and falls in unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. The covers remain locked until the puzzle cube is moved from the pedestal in area 6C.

detection.detail: A character who searches the hallway floor for traps finds a pit trap with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: magic such as an arcane lock spell
disarm.detail: The lids are cleverly constructed and can be jammed shut only by using magic such as an arcane lock spell.

effect: A creature stepping on a pit cover causes it to swing open and falls in unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. Each pit is 10 feet deep and has a patch of green slime (see chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide) at the bottom of it.
area: Three covered pits spaced along the corridor in the positions marked X on the shrine map.
description: Three covered pits are spaced along the corridor. Their covers remain locked until the puzzle cube is moved from the pedestal in area 6C. Each pit is 10 feet deep and has a patch of green slime at the bottom.

name: Unkh's Shrine Pedestal Trap
trigger: A character inserts the wrong key into the keyhole at the base of the pedestal or botches an attempt to pick the lock (fails the DC 25 Dexterity check by 5 or more).

detection.detail: No detection method specified in the source text.

disarm.detail: Using thieves' tools, a character can pick the lock on the pedestal with a successful DC 25 Dexterity check. A character who fails the check by 5 or more accidentally triggers the trap.

effect: The shell of the flail snail statue emits dazzling rays of light that fire in all directions. Each creature in the shrine must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. Any creature that fails the save is struck by a ray and takes 33 (6d10) radiant damage. The statue can't emit rays while wholly or partly contained within an antimagic field.
description: A trap on the pedestal in Unkh's shrine that fires dazzling rays of light from the flail snail statue when the wrong key is inserted or the lock is botched.

name: Axe Blade Trap
trigger: If more than 20 pounds of pressure is exerted on a pressure plate, a sharpened axe blade swings from a hidden compartment in the ceiling.

detection.detail: A character searching for traps spots a pressure plate and ceiling compartment with a successful DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Wedging an iron spike or other object under a plate prevents the trap from triggering. Using thieves' tools, a character can dismantle an axe blade with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. If the check fails by 5 or more, the trap triggers and makes an attack against the character with disadvantage.

effect: The blade makes a melee attack (+6 to hit) against any creature standing on the pressure plate. On a hit, the target takes 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
area: Any creature standing on the pressure plate
description: Hidden pressure plates in the floor trigger a sharpened axe blade from the ceiling in a dusty maze.

name: Puzzle Cube Trap
trigger: Any creature that touches the puzzle cube

disarm.detail: When the torches in this room are inserted into the empty brackets in area 19B, Obo'laka's puzzle cube can be handled safely.

effect: Any creature that touches the puzzle cube must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be petrified. Even on a success, a creature holding the cube must repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns until the puzzle cube is removed from the shrine.
description: A magical trap on a puzzle cube that petrifies creatures that touch it.

name: Soporific Gas Trap
trigger: Pressing the stone button (black opal) in Ras Nsi's crown on the wall relief

detection.detail: A character who searches the reliefs and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check discovers that the black opal in Ras Nsi's crown is a stone button. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the character also sees tiny holes hidden among the scales of the Night Serpent carvings.

disarm.method: Plug the holes with cloth or wax
disarm.detail: Using cloth or wax, characters can plug the hundreds of holes and prevent the gas from flowing out.

effect: The carvings of the Night Serpent expel a soporific gas that fills the hallway and lingers for 1 minute. Any creature that moves into the gas or starts its turn inside it must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. The gas has no effect on creatures that cannot be poisoned, and creatures that fail the save fall unconscious for 1 hour.
description: A hidden button in a wall relief triggers a soporific gas that fills the hallway, knocking creatures unconscious.

name: Poison Needle Trap
trigger: A character who tries to pick the lock without first disabling the trap

detection.detail: Finding the trap requires a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check

disarm.detail: once found, it can be disabled with a successful DC 12 Dexterity check

effect: The character is pricked by the needle, takes 5 (1d10) poison damage, and is blinded. The blindness is permanent but can be cured with a lesser restoration spell or similar magic.
area: The lock on the south door
description: The south door is locked, and the lock contains a cleverly hidden poison needle trap.

name: False Entrance Gas Trap
trigger: Inserting puzzle cubes representing every trickster god except Unkh into the cavities in such a way that the cubes of rival gods are opposite to one another causes a stone block to slowly descend over the tunnel entrance.

detection.detail: Any character searching the tunnel for traps spots the raised stone block with a successful DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: Dexterity check (six successful checks, each made as an action)
disarm.detail: Stuffing the holes in the mouths of the skulls with cloth or wax prevents the gas from being released. Doing so while the trap is active is difficult, requiring six successful DC 10 Dexterity checks, each made as an action.

effect: A stone block slowly descends over the tunnel entrance. Any character in the tunnel must decide whether to stay or to flee, which requires a successful DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. Characters who stay or who fail the check are trapped when the stone block seals off the tunnel. Once the tunnel is sealed, caustic gas billows out from the mouths of the relief-carved skulls. Any creature trapped in the tunnel must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (1d10) poison damage and 5 (1d10) acid damage. While any affected creature remains in the tunnel, it must repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns. After 10 rounds, the gas valves close and the stone block rises back into the ceiling. Any puzzle cubes still in their cavities are pushed out, and the trap resets.
area: The tunnel of the false entrance
description: A false entrance to the Tomb of the Nine Gods that seals with a stone block and releases caustic gas when the wrong combination of puzzle cubes is inserted.

name: First Puzzle Door
trigger: A puzzle cube is placed incorrectly in one of the nine cube-shaped cavities.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around each of the cavities.

disarm.detail: The door opens only when all nine puzzle cubes are placed in the proper configuration. A mage hand spell can be used to place the cubes from farther away and avoid the damage.

effect: If a puzzle cube is placed incorrectly, any previously placed cubes pop out. Electricity then erupts from the incorrectly placed cube, dealing 18 (4d8) lightning damage to any creature within 20 feet of the door.
description: A slab of worked stone blocks the overgrown tunnel some twenty feet from the entrance. Grinning skulls mark the edges of the slab, in the center of which are nine cube-shaped cavities arranged in three rows of three. The cubes representing the trickster gods must be placed so that each god is opposite its rival's cube on the grid, with Unkh (who is neutral and has no rivals) in the middle.

name: Magical Attraction
trigger: Any metal object not being worn or carried that enters the room and weighs 150 pounds or less is instantly drawn to the shield. Any creature wearing or carrying metal items that enters the room or starts its turn there can feel the pull of the statue.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of transmutation magic over the shield.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 17) cast on the statue shuts down the attractive field for 1 hour. If the statue and shield are destroyed, the trap is disabled.

effect: Any metal object that comes into direct contact with the shield disintegrates, showering the floor with powdered rust. Artifacts are immune to this corrosion. Any creature wearing or carrying metal items that enters the room or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to resist the pull. On a failed check, the creature loses its footing, flies across the chamber, and slams into the statue, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it moved. If the character is wearing metal armor, the check is made with disadvantage.
area: The hall containing the rusting statue of a knight at the west end
description: A rusting statue of a knight gripping a large iron shield creates a magical field that attracts and disintegrates metal objects.

name: Gas Pocket
trigger: If a torch, lantern, or other open flame is brought into the area, or if the secret door to area 10 is opened, the gas explodes.

detection.detail: The gas has a rotten odor.

disarm.detail: The explosion burns away the gas, which builds up again after 8 hours.

effect: Each creature in the area of the gas pocket or within 15 feet of it must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half damage on a successful one.
area: The area of the gas pocket or within 15 feet of it
description: This section of the underground river contains a buildup of flammable gas that has a rotten odor.

name: Trapped Chest
trigger: Attempting to pick the lock.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around it.

disarm.detail: Picking the lock requires a successful DC 22 Dexterity check made using thieves' tools. This also disarms the lock's magical trap, allowing the chest to be opened safely.

effect: If the check fails, the demon skull bites down on the thieves' tools and destroys them. If the check fails by 5 or more, the magical trap teleports the character making the check inside the locked chest, whereupon the character is restrained. The chains holding the chest then release it into the water, where it sinks to the bottom of the pool. Even if the chest is removed from the water, a character trapped within runs out of air after 5 rounds (see "Suffocating" in chapter 8 of the Player's Handbook).
description: The chest is locked and doesn't appear to be trapped. However, a detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around it.

name: Stone Skull
trigger: Each time a creature climbs through the skull's jaws, one of the flames in its eye sockets snuffs out. The third time a creature climbs through, the jaws clamp shut.

detection.detail: Any character searching the skull and succeeding on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notes that the lower jaw is hinged.

disarm.method: jam a stout object into the skull's jaw
disarm.detail: A stout object jammed into the skull's jaw holds it open for as long as the object can withstand the damage.

effect: The jaws clamp shut, making a melee weapon attack with a +10 bonus. On a hit, the target creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and is grappled (escape DC 19). While it remains grappled, the creature takes 5 (1d10) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. When that creature exits the jaws, the flames in the skull's eye sockets reignite, the jaws open, and the trap resets.
description: A giant stone skull crusted with moss juts out from the end of the passageway. A flame flickers within each of its eye sockets, and a view into a chamber beyond can be seen through its open jaws.

name: Wind Tunnel Propeller
trigger: whenever more than 20 pounds of pressure is placed on the corridor floor

detection.detail: a character discerns that the entire floor of the corridor is a single pressure plate

disarm.detail: While the propeller is motionless, a creature that isn't incapacitated can jam the mechanism with its body. When the propeller begins to turn, the creature must make a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. If the check succeeds, the propeller is jammed until the start of the creature's next turn, when it can use its action to repeat the check. If the propeller is jammed for 3 consecutive rounds, it breaks down and becomes nonfunctional.

effect: The adamantine propeller thunders into motion, spinning up to full speed in 6 seconds. While spinning up or slowing down, a creature can leap through a gap between two blades with a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check; on a failed check, the character takes 33 (6d10) slashing damage. At full speed, the propeller deals 66 (12d10) slashing damage to any creature that passes through it, and the blades are turning too fast for a creature to leap between them. The rapidly spinning propeller also creates a wind tunnel effect, such that any creature that comes within 10 feet of the propeller or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw. A creature that fails the save is hurled northward into the pit in area 16. If this forced movement causes the creature to pass through the propeller, the creature takes damage from the spinning blades. One can jam the propeller by fixing an immovable rod in place between two of the blades. Other magic items wedged between the blades are knocked aside as the propeller turns. The propeller destroys all nonmagical objects lodged between its spinning blades. A creature that fails the check or chooses to extricate itself takes 11 (2d10) slashing damage and is ejected north of the propeller.
description: A large adamantine propeller with five sharp blades blocks the passage. The entire floor is a pressure plate that activates the propeller.

name: Onyx Chest Trap
trigger: Pushing the onyx button on Wongo's sarcophagus
effect: forces any creature inside the onyx chest to succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 75 (10d6 + 40) force damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage turns to a pile of dust, leaving behind whatever gear it was holding or wearing.
description: A trap within the onyx chest that triggers when the corresponding button on Wongo's sarcophagus is pressed.

name: Onyx Chest Button Trap
trigger: Pushing the onyx button on the sarcophagus lid
effect: Pushing the onyx button forces any creature inside the onyx chest to succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 75 (10d6 + 40) force damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage turns to a pile of dust, leaving behind whatever gear it was holding or wearing.
description: A trap triggered by pressing the onyx button on the sarcophagus lid, affecting creatures inside the onyx chest.

name: Rusty Iron Chest Button Trap
trigger: Pushing the rusty iron button on the sarcophagus lid
effect: Pushing the rusty iron button causes any nonmagical metal objects inside the rusty iron chest (including objects carried or worn by a creature in the chest) to corrode into worthless piles of rust. Objects partly made of metal are ruined as their metal components decay.
area: Nonmagical metal objects inside the rusty iron chest
description: A trap triggered by pressing the rusty iron button on the sarcophagus lid, corroding metal objects inside the rusty iron chest.

name: Silver Chest Button Trap
trigger: Pushing the silver button on the sarcophagus lid
effect: Pushing the silver button causes any creature inside the silver chest to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A trap triggered by pressing the silver button on the sarcophagus lid, affecting creatures inside the silver chest.

name: Slippery Ledge
trigger: Taking damage while standing on the ledge
effect: Any creature that takes damage while standing on the ledge must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall into the rift, plunging 100 feet into the water at area 64. The fall deals 35 (10d6) bludgeoning damage, or no damage with a successful DC 10 Dexterity saving throw.
description: A slippery and uneven ledge that can cause creatures to fall into a rift.

name: False Tomb Trap
trigger: If the illusory sunlight falling from the ceiling strikes the plaque when the coffin is opened, the stone block in the corridor outside the room slowly descends, sealing the entrance in 6 seconds.

detection.detail: A character who searches the tunnel spots the block with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Casting dispel magic on the illusory sunlight dispels it and prevents the trap from triggering.

effect: The stone block descends, sealing the entrance. A creature that wishes to enter or leave the tomb during this time can do so, moving up to its speed. If the creature ends its movement under the block, it must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. If the save succeeds, the creature manages to get out from under the block on the side it was moving toward. If the save fails, the creature takes 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. If this damage reduces the creature's hit points to 0, it is crushed to a pulp; otherwise, the creature is shoved into the room. The block is impervious to damage and spells. When fully lowered, the block is airtight and refuses to be budged. Four enormous cisterns filled with red wine are hidden in the walls behind the gargoyle heads. When the stone block seals off the entrance, the valves behind the heads open, causing the wine to pour from the gargoyles' mouths and nostrils. The wine floods the tomb at a rate of 1 foot per round. Trying to crawl into a gargoyle's mouth while wine is gushing out of it requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check. As the wine begins pouring into the room, all creatures present must roll initiative. Track the passage of rounds: At the start of round 3, three wine weirds (use water weird statistics) flow into the tomb from the northwest, northeast, and southeast cisterns. The weirds attack anyone in the tomb and are invisible while fully immersed in wine. After 12 rounds, the wine fills the tomb. Use the underwater combat rules in chapter 9 of the Player's Handbook to handle fighting in these conditions. Visibility within the wine is limited to 5 feet. The ability to breathe water does not help a character drowning in wine. When 10 minutes have passed, the stone block sealing the tomb rises back up to its niche in the ceiling. The wine cascades down the west tunnel, pouring down the grand staircase (area 7). At dawn the next day, Withers sends tomb dwarves to clean up the room and tunnel, after which the wine cisterns magically refill and the trap resets.
description: A trap in the False Tomb that seals the entrance with a stone block and floods the room with wine.

name: Alien Growth
trigger: Any effect that deals fire, necrotic, or radiant damage destroys a patch of alien growth on contact.

detection.detail: The beholder's aberrant influence permeates the stonework across this level of the tomb, causing purple mold to sprout from the floors, walls, and ceilings. The mold smells like rotting corpses and occasionally releases clouds of harmless spores. As characters move through areas with alien growth, tiny eyeballs emerge from the mold to scrutinize them.

effect: When a patch of growth is destroyed, the next nearest patch sprouts a stubby eyestalk that shoots a randomly determined eye ray at the nearest character. (Roll a d10 and consult the beholder stat block to determine which ray it produces.) After making this attack, the eyestalk quickly disappears back into the mold.
description: The beholder's aberrant influence permeates the stonework across this level of the tomb, causing purple mold to sprout from the floors, walls, and ceilings.

name: Iron Barrier
trigger: The barrier snaps down after 1 minute unless it is wedged in place with an iron spike, a stout weapon, or a similar object. Any creature underneath the sheet when it snaps shut is subject to the trap's effect.

detection.detail: Any character who examines the barrier discovers that it slides up into the ceiling.

disarm.detail: The barrier can be wedged in place with an iron spike, a stout weapon, or a similar object to prevent it from snapping down.

effect: Any creature underneath the sheet when it snaps shut must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 44 (8d10) slashing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is chopped in two.
area: The crawlway blocked by the iron sheet.
description: A 1-inch-thick, sharp-edged iron sheet etched with a snarling minotaur face blocks the crawlway. It can be lifted with a successful DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check, but snaps down after 1 minute unless wedged in place.

name: Curtain of Water
trigger: Any creature passes through the curtain without a trident.

detection.detail: Radiates an aura of conjuration magic to a detect magic spell or similar effect.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 17) cast on the curtain causes it to vanish, leaving the archway open. The curtain magically reappears after 1 hour.

effect: The water erupts as a fierce wave flowing north and south. Any creature in either hall is slammed by the water and must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature takes 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and is swept to the end of the hall with such great force that it falls prone. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw takes half damage and falls prone, but is not swept away.
area: Both hallways connected by the curtain of water.
description: A 1-foot-thick, 7-foot-high, 10-foot-wide curtain of clear water separates two hallways. Passing through with a trident is safe; without one, the water erupts into a fierce wave.

name: Rotating Crawlways
trigger: When 50 pounds or more of weight is applied to the floor at the midpoint of tunnel A, a mechanism causes the tunnel to quickly rotate 90 degrees clockwise and sink 5 feet as it turns.

detection.detail: Any character searching for traps or secret doors in this tunnel notices a narrow seam in the stonework with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the character can deduce that the seam represents a point where two sections of tunnel can detach from one another.

effect: Both ends of the tunnel are immediately cut off, trapping creatures inside. At the same time, a second crawlway perpendicular to the first (marked "Tunnel B" on map 5.3) rotates 90 degrees clockwise and sinks into place, positioned where tunnel A used to be. Characters who are flying, in gaseous form, or otherwise effectively weightless do not trigger the trap and can move through the tunnel safely. When tunnel B connects to the rest of the crawlway, a new passage running north to south is formed. Tunnel B is trapped similarly to tunnel A, except that both tunnels ascend 5 feet as they rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise when the trap triggers. The only way to return tunnel A to its original position is to trigger the trap from tunnel B, and vice versa. Characters trapped in a section of tunnel not connected to the rest of the crawlway have no clear means of escape. The tunnel is airtight. A single creature consumes the available air supply in 24 hours, with multiple creatures dividing that time up between them.
area: 25-foot-long section of crawlway (Tunnel A) and a second crawlway (Tunnel B)
description: A rotating crawlway trap that traps creatures inside an airtight tunnel.

name: Corrosive Gas Trap
trigger: Removing the dial from its spoke inside the stone block releases a corrosive gas trapped within the block.

detection.detail: A character who searches for traps can detect the holes hidden behind the dial with a DC 25 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Once found, these holes can be plugged with wax before the dial is removed, preventing the gas from escaping.

effect: The gas escapes through tiny holes hidden behind the dial and fills the 5-foot space directly east of the block. Any creature in this area when the gas is released must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw, taking 44 (8d10) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: 5-foot space directly east of the block
description: A corrosive gas trap hidden behind a gold medallion and clay dial in area 35A.

name: Hieroglyphic Floor Trap
trigger: Stepping on a floor tile that does not match the correct sequence of hieroglyphs.

detection.detail: The correct sequence is revealed by the clay dial in area 35A; no specific detection check is mentioned.

disarm.detail: Stepping on the tiles in the correct order disables the trap. After 24 hours, Withers sends 1d4 tomb dwarves to reset the trap.

effect: When any creature steps on an incorrect floor tile, all four sphinx statues yawn and masses of magically summoned locusts fly out of their mouths. The locusts form a single cloud that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile. Each creature in the cloud when it forms, as well as any creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this trap is killed and eaten to the bone by the devouring locusts.
area: 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile
description: A trap in area 35B that triggers when floor tiles are stepped on in the wrong order, summoning a cloud of locusts from sphinx statues.

name: Stone Block Ceiling Trap
trigger: Stepping onto any floor tile in area 35B while the passage to the east is open causes the stone block at area 35A to rise and seal the tunnel.

detection.detail: No specific detection check is mentioned.

disarm.detail: No specific disarm method is mentioned.

effect: Any creature atop the block when it meets the ceiling must succeed on a DC 7 Dexterity saving throw to leap clear in one direction or the other. On a failed save, the creature takes 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is crushed to a pulp. Otherwise, the creature falls prone inside the tomb.
description: A trap where a stone block rises to seal a tunnel, potentially crushing creatures atop it.

name: Devouring Locusts
trigger: Stepping on the offending floor tile
effect: The locusts form a single cloud that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile. Each creature in the cloud when it forms, as well as any creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this trap is killed and eaten to the bone by the devouring locusts. The cloud lasts for 1 minute or until another cloud of locusts is created.
area: 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile
description: A trap that releases a cloud of devouring locusts when a specific floor tile is stepped on.

name: Wailing Winds
trigger: Pulling the lever on the west balcony

disarm.method: Returning the lever to its original up position
disarm.detail: Returning the lever to its original up position causes the winds to abate and the statue's fists to close.

effect: Howling winds rise up and fill the room. While the winds are howling, any creature not standing on a floating platform that starts its turn in the room must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or gain a random form of short-term madness, determined by rolling on the Short-Term Madness table in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide. Constructs and undead are immune to this madness. In addition, the winds cause creatures in the room to suffer disadvantage on all Strength-based skill checks, including checks made to jump to and from the floating platforms and checks made to climb the walls.
description: A trap triggered by a lever that fills the room with howling winds causing madness and hindering Strength checks.

name: Revolving Room
trigger: The room revolves, knocking about any creature not firmly attached to a wall, flying, or under the effect of a gaseous form spell or similar magic.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: The room stops tumbling if the lever in area 38A is raised, or if the south door is opened or destroyed. The door's locks are hidden in the walls and can't be picked with thieves' tools, and it takes three separate knock spells to unlock them. The door can also be wrenched open with a successful DC 26 Strength (Athletics) check or attacked. It has AC 17; 50 hit points; and immunity to fire, piercing, poison, psychic, slashing, and thunder damage.

effect: At the start of each of its turns, a creature in the room must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. While the room is revolving, an additional effect is triggered at the end of initiative count 10. Roll a d20 and consult the Revolving Room Effects table.
description: A revolving room that knocks creatures about and triggers random effects.

name: Revolving Room Effects
trigger: Triggered at the end of initiative count 10 while the room is revolving.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: Roll a d20 and consult the Revolving Room Effects table: 1-6: The demon faces exhale jets of a soporific gas that dissipates quickly. Each creature in the room that is not immune to the poisoned condition must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious. An unconscious creature can repeat the saving throw each time it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. 7-12: The demon faces exhale jets of sparkling dust, which blind any creature in the room that does not succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. A creature's blindness lasts until it is cured with a lesser restoration spell or similar magic. 13-18: Stone spikes 6 inches long magically protrude from the walls. Any creature that takes damage from the room at the start of its turn takes an additional 11 (2d10) piercing damage from the spikes. The spikes retract when the next room effect is triggered. 19-20: The demon faces spew jets of an incendiary gas that promptly ignites, filling the room with fire. Each creature in the room takes 45 (10d8) fire damage.
description: Random effects triggered by the revolving room.

name: Golem Pit
trigger: Entering the area or manipulating the statues.

detection.detail: Either statue can be identified with a successful DC 12 Intelligence (Religion) check. A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of abjuration magic around each statue.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: An invisible wall of force covers the top of the pit. By manipulating the statues, characters can teleport the golem up to their level, or send one of their own into the pit. Rotating the statue of Azuth to the right teleports one creature inside the pit onto the third plinth. Rotating the statue of Torm to the right teleports anything on or above the third plinth into the pit. The clay golem has orders to attack any creature that it sees and can reach.
description: A pit containing a clay golem and a stone chest, with statues that teleport creatures.

name: Stone Chest
trigger: Opening the chest by any means other than the silver key.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: A character using thieves' tools can pick the lock with a successful DC 20 Dexterity check.

effect: Releases a cloud of gas that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the chest (filling the entire pit). The gas instantly corrodes and destroys all nonmagical metal that comes into contact with it, including armor and weapons. Metal objects sealed in containers are protected.
description: A stone chest that releases a corrosive gas if opened without the silver key.

name: Sarcophagus Arcane Lock Trap
trigger: Opening the sarcophagus by any means other than the ritual

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals auras of abjuration and evocation magic around the sarcophagus.

disarm.detail: Can be opened with a knock spell or forced open with a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check, but doing so triggers the trap.

effect: A prismatic spray spell (save DC 19) erupts from the wall behind the sarcophagus. All creatures in the room, as well as creatures in the narrow hallway to the south, become targets of the spell.
area: All creatures in the room, as well as creatures in the narrow hallway to the south
description: The sarcophagus lid is sealed shut with an arcane lock spell. If opened by any means other than the ritual, a prismatic spray spell erupts.

name: Wraith Ambush
trigger: Performing any of the ritual actions incorrectly
effect: Three wraiths rise from the bones on the floor. The wraiths attack until they are destroyed and pursue any characters who flee this area. When the wraiths appear, any character wearing one of the frog masks is polymorphed into a frog, as though it had failed a saving throw against the polymorph spell.
description: If any ritual actions are performed incorrectly, three wraiths rise from the bones on the floor and attack.

name: Third Curtain of the Feast Hall
trigger: Any creature that looks at this curtain

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of enchantment magic radiating from the third curtain.

effect: Any creature that looks at this curtain must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of it. A frightened creature tries to leave the room as quickly as possible and cannot reenter. Once outside the room, a creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that saves against this effect is unaffected by the curtain thereafter and can reenter the room.
description: An enchanted curtain that frightens creatures that look upon it.

name: Lord of the Feast (Severed Boar's Head)
trigger: Any humanoid that can see the severed boar's head

detection.detail: The rotting head of a giant boar is mounted to the wall behind the final curtain. Fresh blood and gore spatters its tusks, dribbling down the wall beneath it.

disarm.detail: Destroying the Lord of the Feast ends its charm effect on all creatures. The boar's head is a Medium object with AC 5 and 22 hit points.

effect: Any humanoid that can see the severed boar's head must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by it. On its turn, a charmed creature does nothing except approach the severed head and put its own head in the boar's mouth. Only one head can fit in the mouth at a time. If the boar's mouth is already full, a charmed creature waits patiently until the mouth is clear. Any creature that ends its turn with its head in the boar's mouth takes 22 (4d10) slashing damage as the boar's jaws clamp down. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated. A charmed creature can repeat the saving throw each time it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once a creature successfully saves against this effect, it cannot be affected by the boar's head for 24 hours.
area: Line of sight to the boar's head
description: A severed boar's head that charms humanoids into placing their heads in its mouth, clamping down and decapitating them.

name: Slick Vault Floor
trigger: Any creature that steps onto or starts its turn on the floor

detection.detail: The floor beneath the dome is magically slick.

effect: Any creature that steps onto or starts its turn on the floor must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. When an untethered creature is shoved or otherwise moved across the floor, it travels in one direction and does not stop until it comes into contact with a wall or other barrier.
area: The floor beneath the dome in the Vault of the Beholder
description: A magically slick floor that causes creatures to fall prone and slide uncontrollably.

name: Lava Trap
trigger: Molten lava begins pouring from the tiny holes in the ceiling as soon as any character comes within 1 foot of the candle or removes it from the sconce.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: The lava rains down and magically drains away through the holes in the floor. Each creature in the cell when the lava begins to fall must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Any creature that enters the cell for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must repeat the saving throw. Because of the cell's antimagic field, magic items and spells that provide resistance to fire offer no protection here.
description: A trap that pours molten lava from ceiling holes when the candle is approached or removed.

name: Flood Trap
trigger: The water begins to pour into the cell through rows of tiny holes in the ten-foot-high ceiling when characters appear in the cell.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: Trying to stuff or block the holes doesn't stop the water from pouring in.

effect: The water fills the cell at a rate of 1 foot per round, taking 10 rounds to fill the room. If the candle is left in its sconce, the rising water extinguishes it on the fourth round. Because of the cell's antimagic field, spells and magic items that enable characters to breathe underwater don't function here. Any character who runs out of air begins to suffocate.
description: A trap that floods the cell with water, risking suffocation.

name: Falling Sand Pit Trap
trigger: The falling sand fills the room at a rate of 6 inches per round. If the sand reaches a depth of 12 inches, the floor splits open along its seam.

detection.detail: Any character who searches the cell and succeeds on a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check notices a seam running down the middle of the floor from north to south.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified. Characters can stuff holes with cloth or wax to slow the sand by 1 inch per round.

effect: When the pit opens, half of the floor swings down to the west and the other half drops to the east, and the sand stops falling. A 6-inch-wide ledge surrounds the pit on all sides. Any creature standing on the floor when it opens must make a DC 15 Dexterity check; those standing along the walls have advantage on the check. On a successful save, a creature finds purchase on the ledge. A creature that fails the save falls. The 10-foot-deep pit contains two giant stone rollers with interlocking stone teeth. Anything larger than a grain of sand gets chewed up between these rollers, taking 132 (24d10) force damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is ground to a pulp. A creature that passes through the rollers with at least 1 hit point remaining lands on an iron grate 5 feet below the grinders. A stone button is set into one of the walls above the grate and is visible only to creatures under the rollers. When pressed, the button causes the rollers to stop turning and retract into the walls, allowing creatures that survived the horrid trap to climb out with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
description: A pit trap in a cell where sand fills the room, eventually causing the floor to split open and drop creatures into a pit with grinding stone rollers.

name: Sphere of Annihilation in Devil Face
trigger: Any character who stands within 5 feet of the sphere can hear a faint whisper emanating from it.

detection.detail: A successful DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check allows a character to make out words in Abyssal that translate as follows: "Darkness is coming for you. Your doom is at hand."

disarm.detail: The sphere of annihilation can't be controlled or moved.

effect: The darkness within the mouth is a sphere of annihilation, which can't be controlled or moved.
description: A green stone face of devilish countenance protrudes from the wall. The devil's mouth is agape and filled with darkness. The devil face is 6 feet tall, with a mouth 2 feet in diameter. A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of transmutation magic on the face.

name: Mirror of Life Trapping
trigger: Any creature within 30 feet of the mirror that sees its reflection

detection.detail: Casting an identify spell on the mirror reveals its command words and magical properties.

disarm.detail: Speaking the word "Khomara" while standing within 5 feet of the mirror deactivates or reactivates it.

effect: Any creature within 30 feet of the mirror that sees its reflection must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be imprisoned within one of the mirror's twelve extradimensional cells, along with anything it is wearing or carrying. Constructs automatically succeed on the saving throw.
description: This dusty room is fifteen feet square and empty except for an ornate, rectangular mirror mounted on the wall opposite the room's only exit. Attached to the west wall with sovereign glue is a mirror of life trapping.

name: Golden Sun
trigger: Whenever the sun or its chain are touched or damaged, the sun's smile fades to an inscrutable expression, and it emits tremendous heat in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on itself. The first time the queen's remains or any of her treasures are removed from the sarcophagus, the sun's expression turns angry as it emits rays of searing light.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals auras of evocation magic around the golden sun.

disarm.detail: The sun and its chain are treated as a single Small object with AC 15; 22 hit points; and immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage. The sun loses its magical properties when it shoots its rays or is destroyed.

effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the area takes 10 (3d6) fire damage. This effect ends if all creatures leave the affected area. When the queen's remains or treasures are removed, each creature within 30 feet of the sun that doesn't have total cover against it must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be struck by a ray, which deals 42 (12d6) fire damage.
area: 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the sun; 30 feet for rays
description: A two-foot-diameter orb hanging from a chain above the sarcophagus, made of hammered gold to resemble a smiling sun. It emits tremendous heat when touched or damaged, and shoots searing rays when the queen's remains or treasures are removed.

name: Napaka's Baleful Gas
trigger: If the scepter is removed and not immediately replaced with its nonmagical twin from area 52, or if Napaka's remains are removed from their resting place, the queen's corpse opens its mouth in a wide yawn and exhales a baleful black gas.

disarm.detail: Replacing the scepter with its nonmagical twin from area 52, or not removing Napaka's remains, prevents the trap.

effect: The gas fills a 15-foot cube centered on the corpse. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (7d12) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A magical trap triggered by removing Napaka's scepter or remains, causing her corpse to exhale a baleful black gas.

name: Rolling Doom (Granite Ball)
trigger: When the chest or its lid is lifted, a heavy stone ball tumbles down the stairs.

detection.detail: Finding the compartment requires that a character search the tunnel ceiling and succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The hatch can be jammed with an iron spike or with a successful DC 20 Dexterity check made using thieves' tools.

effect: When released, the stone ball thunders down the stairs and tumbles into the pit at 54C. Any character on the stairs or in the tunnel below can stay ahead of the ball by running toward the pit. A character can also leap over the ball with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. Any character who fails the check or can't move out of the ball's way is struck for 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and knocked prone. The ball also flattens the treasure chest (54A) as it tumbles through.
description: A 5-foot-diameter sphere of solid granite balances within a secret compartment at the top of the stairs, released when the treasure chest is lifted.

name: Acid Pit
trigger: The pit's lid is crafted of interlocking stone tiles that fall apart beneath 100 pounds or more of weight.

detection.detail: Any character who searches the floor notices the unusual stonework and smells the acid below with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: A creature in the area of the pit when the floor collapses can avoid a fall and grab the edge of the pit with a successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. The saving throw is made with disadvantage if the character was unaware of the pit. Any creature that enters the acid for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 66 (12d10) acid damage. The walls of the pit are too smooth to climb without the aid of magic or climbing gear.
area: 10-foot-deep pit, filled with green acid to a depth of 5 feet
description: A 10-foot-deep pit with glass-lined walls filled with green acid, hidden beneath interlocking stone tiles.

name: Grandfather Clock
trigger: Any creature within 30 feet of the clock when it strikes the top of the hour

detection.detail: This long-case clock radiates an aura of transmutation magic to a detect magic spell or similar effect.

disarm.detail: To pick the lock, a character must succeed on a DC 20 Dexterity check made using thieves' tools. If the character thinks to blow powdered chalk, dust, or a similar substance into the lock to highlight its gears, the check is made with advantage. The invisible key from the treasure chest in area 54A opens the lock, as does a knock spell.

effect: Any creature within 30 feet of the clock when it strikes the top of the hour must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or age by ten years. The effect can be reversed by a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.
description: A long-case clock that ages creatures when it chimes the hour.

name: Green Devil Face
trigger: Pulling the lever in the left nostril

detection.detail: Any close inspection reveals that its nostrils contain hollow cavities, each one containing a stone lever.

disarm.detail: A pulled lever locks into place and can't be moved until it resets. After 1 minute, the lever resets with an audible clunk.

effect: Pulling the lever in the left nostril causes the mouth of the devil face to open wide, revealing a gullet filled with impenetrable darkness that pulls in everything in the room. Initiative should be rolled for all creatures in the area. Any creature that starts its turn in the room and isn't secured in some fashion must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw or be pulled into the gullet and destroyed. If a character fails the saving throw, another character within reach, or any character bound to the first character by a rope, can use his or her reaction to grab on and grant the first character a reroll. After 1 minute, the lever resets with an audible clunk. The gullet remains open until the lever resets. Magic has no effect on the gullet or the darkness within.
description: An 8-foot-high devil face with levers in its nostrils that can pull creatures into a dark gullet or teleport them.

name: Aboleth Slime
trigger: Any creature that starts its turn in a puddle of slime or comes into contact with it for the first time on a turn

detection.detail: Puddles of viscid gray slime cover the floor in some areas, as marked on map 5.5.

disarm.detail: A slime puddle is destroyed if it takes any cold, radiant, or necrotic damage. It is immune to all other types of damage.

effect: These areas are difficult terrain, and any creature that starts its turn in a puddle of slime or comes into contact with it for the first time on a turn takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage.
description: Puddles of viscid gray slime that damage creatures entering them.

name: Poisonous Gas
trigger: Starting turn in a gas-filled area

disarm.detail: Stuffing the nozzles with cloth prevents more gas from spilling into the room.

effect: Any creature susceptible to the gas that starts its turn in a gas-filled area must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature is affected even if it holds its breath or doesn't need to breathe.
description: Thick green gas billows out of skull-shaped nozzles set into the walls of this cramped room.

name: Falling Stone Block
trigger: Inserting the gold lever into the star-shaped indentation on the back of the golden mastodon's head.

detection.detail: A character who searches for traps in the tunnel approaching the room notices a block of stone lodged in the ceiling with a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described.

effect: A thunderous trumpeting sound erupts from the mastodon's trunk, causing a block of stone to seal off the room. The block of stone fills the space in the hallway indicated on map 5.5.
