Any creature under the block when it falls must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a success, the creature moves out of the block's way in whichever direction it prefers. On a failed save, the creature takes 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. If this damage reduces the creature's hit points to 0, the creature is crushed to a pulp; otherwise, it is shoved into the room.
area: The space in the hallway indicated on map 5.5, under the falling block.
description: A block of stone lodged in the ceiling falls when the golden mastodon trap is activated.

name: Revolving Mastodon Statue
trigger: When the mastodon statue begins to revolve, all creatures present should roll initiative. The statue turns counterclockwise and completes one 360-degree revolution on initiative count 0 of each round.
effect: When the statue completes its first revolution, magical fire engulfs the floor and the cog, flaring up 6 feet high. Any creature that enters the fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 10 (3d6) fire damage. Any character perched on the golden mastodon is shielded from the flames. Up to six Medium creatures can perch on the mastodon at once-four on its back and one on each of its curved tusks. Each time the statue turns to face north, one or more devils emerge from the murals and attack all other creatures in the room. Roll initiative for each group of new arrivals. Each magically summoned devil vanishes in a puff of smoke when it drops to 0 hit points or when there are no creatures left to attack. The devils appear in the following order, emerging from the walls wherever you see fit: Round 2: Four spined devils; Round 3: Three bearded devils; Round 4: Two barbed devils; Round 5: One horned devil; Round 6: One erinyes. If the characters try to strike a bargain with the devils, only the erinyes is willing to engage them- but it demands the willing sacrifice of one character's soul. A character who offers his or her soul to the erinyes is destroyed by fire. The character's soul becomes trapped in the Soulmonger, the character's belongings are left behind, and all remaining devils in the room disappear in clouds of smoke.
description: A revolving mastodon statue that triggers magical fire and summons devils.

name: Hall of Decay
trigger: All nonmagical objects made of cloth, leather, wood, or metal that enter this corridor instantly decay or corrode to the point of being useless and worthless.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of necromancy magic emanating from the ivory ring.

disarm.detail: If the ring is yanked from the skull's jaws, it disintegrates and the destructive effect in the hallway ends.

effect: Clothing and armor falls apart, shields and weapons become brittle and ineffective, and so forth. A mending spell cannot repair an object damaged in this fashion.
description: A hallway that causes nonmagical objects to decay or corrode.

name: Spider Fan Trap
trigger: If a character in the room reads the entire nursery rhyme beginning with the first line on page 1 and ending with the last line on page 8, or if the compartment in the lectern is opened improperly, the ceiling fan begins to twirl as a reverse gravity spell activates within the room.

detection.detail: Any character who inspects the floor of the room and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notices thin seams along the floor's perimeter that suggest a pit below. The seams are meant to deceive adventurers and make them wary of the floor, which doesn't actually have a pit underneath it. The real danger is the ceiling, which appears to be smooth-cut stone but is actually thin plaster.

disarm.detail: The trap does not reset. No disarm method is specified in the source text.

effect: The ceiling fan begins to twirl as a reverse gravity spell activates within the room. The lectern is the only fixed object in the room. Any creature within reach of it can, with a successful DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, grab the lectern and avoid falling upward. A creature that can't grab the lectern or isn't secured in some other way "falls" upward through the fake plaster ceiling into the rotating blades of the fan, taking 44 (8d10) slashing damage. The creature takes that damage again each time it starts its turn on the ceiling. The reverse gravity effect lasts for 1 minute, after which creatures on the ceiling fall back down to the floor 20 feet below. Once the spell ends, the ceiling fan stops twirling.
area: The room (ceiling fan and reverse gravity effect)
description: A trap in the Trial of the Octagon room where reading the nursery rhyme forward or improperly opening the lectern compartment activates a reverse gravity effect and a spinning blade fan shaped like a giant iron spider mounted on the true ceiling.

name: Glyph of Warding
trigger: Opening the secret door triggers a glyph of warding spell, which targets all creatures in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the door. The sphere spreads around corners.

detection.detail: The triggering glyph is at the bottom right corner of the door and can be found with a successful DC 24 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

effect: Each creature in the area must make a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (5d8) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A glyph of warding spell protects the secret door, triggering when the door is opened.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Gap
trigger: You come to a 10-foot-wide gap between rooftops.

detection.detail: The gap is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must be crossed.

effect: You can jump over the gap if your Strength is 10 or higher (each foot you clear costs 1 foot of movement), and you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or fall prone on the far rooftop. Or you can cross the gap using a 10-foot-long rope line that stretches between the two rooftops; each foot of rope line costs 2 feet of movement.
description: A gap between rooftops that must be jumped or crossed via rope.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Higher Rooftop
trigger: You come to a rooftop that's 10 feet higher than the one you're on.

detection.detail: The height change is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must be climbed.

effect: Make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. On a failed check, the height change counts as 10 feet of difficult terrain.
description: A rooftop that is 10 feet higher than the current one.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Lower Rooftop
trigger: You come to a rooftop that's 10 feet lower than the one you're on.

detection.detail: The height change is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must be jumped down.

effect: Make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to jump down safely. On a failed check, you take damage from the fall and land prone.
description: A rooftop that is 10 feet lower than the current one.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Slippery Roof
trigger: A roof is slippery.

detection.detail: The slippery roof is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must be traversed carefully.

effect: Make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, you fall prone.
description: A slippery roof that can cause a fall.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Rotten Roof
trigger: You step on a rotten section of roof, and it collapses underneath you.

detection.detail: The rotten section is not obvious until stepped on.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must escape after falling.

effect: Make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, you fall partway into the hole in the roof and become stuck. While stuck, you are prone and restrained. You can use an action on your turn to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, ending the effect on a success.
description: A rotten roof section that collapses, trapping the character.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Loose Shingles
trigger: Roof shingles or tiles give way as you step on them.

detection.detail: The loose shingles are not obvious until stepped on.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must maintain balance.

effect: Make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, you fall prone and slide 10 feet back.
description: Loose shingles that cause a fall and slide.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Obstacle
trigger: A rooftop protuberance such as a chimney or weather vane gets in your way.

detection.detail: The obstacle is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must navigate around.

effect: Make a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On a failed check, the obstacle counts as 5 feet of difficult terrain.
description: A chimney or weather vane that impedes movement.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Startled Birds
trigger: You startle a flock of birds nesting on the rooftop, and they flutter all around you.

detection.detail: The birds are obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must push through.

effect: Make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the birds count as 10 feet of difficult terrain.
description: A flock of birds that distracts and impedes movement.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Glyph of Warding
trigger: You trigger a glyph of warding spell placed on the roof to discourage burglars.

detection.detail: The glyph is not obvious until triggered.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must resist the effect.

effect: Make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you are targeted by a Tasha's hideous laughter spell, the effect of which lasts 1 minute.
description: A glyph of warding that casts Tasha's hideous laughter on a failed save.

name: Rooftop Chase Complication: Projectile
trigger: Someone on the ground throws a rock, a snowball, or a similar projectile at you.

detection.detail: The projectile is obvious.

disarm.detail: No disarm; must dodge.

effect: Make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the attack deals no damage but distracts you and counts as 5 feet of difficult terrain.
description: A thrown projectile that distracts and impedes movement.

name: Unstable Bridge
trigger: More than 150 pounds of weight is applied to the bridge

detection.detail: No detection method specified

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified

effect: The bridge collapses. A creature standing on a section of bridge when it collapses must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or fall 60 feet to the floor below.
description: An unstable bridge that collapses under sufficient weight, causing creatures to fall.

name: Middle Bridge Gap
trigger: A character clears the 15-foot-wide gap with a running jump and lands on the bridge

detection.detail: No detection method specified

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified

effect: Part of the bridge breaks away under the character's feet on landing, forcing the character to succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or fall to the floor below.
description: A bridge with a gap that breaks away when landed on after a jump.

name: Enthralling Fresco
trigger: Any creature within 30 feet of the fresco that can see it

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals an aura of enchantment magic on the fresco.

disarm.detail: Destroying at least one 10-foot-square section of the fresco ends the effect for all creatures. Each 10-foot-square section has AC 17, 25 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

effect: Any creature within 30 feet of the fresco that can see it must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by it for 24 hours. While charmed in this way, the creature can't willingly move out of sight of the fresco and defends it to the death. If forcibly moved away from the fresco, the creature tries to find its way back. The creature can't rest while under this effect. After 24 hours, the creature gains one level of exhaustion and can repeat the saving throw if it can still see the fresco, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to the effect of the fresco for 24 hours.
description: A fresco that magically charms creatures that see it.

name: Ol' Fire Eyes Trap
trigger: Anyone who touches the false adamantine trapdoor or its pull ring

detection.detail: A successful DC 17 Intelligence (Religion) check enables a character to recognize the statue as a depiction of Gorm Gulthyn, the dwarven god of vigilance also known as Fire Eyes. A detect magic spell reveals an aura of evocation magic on the statue.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described in the source text.

effect: Rays of magical fire spring from the statue's eyes, dealing 22 (4d10) fire damage. The trap doesn't trigger if the target has total cover.
area: The false trapdoor and its pull ring in area V8
description: A false adamantine trapdoor set into the floor before a statue of Gorm Gulthyn. Touching the trapdoor or its pull ring triggers rays of magical fire from the statue's eyes.

name: Collapsing Maze Trap
trigger: A tripwire rigged halfway through the maze is triggered.

detection.detail: A character in the lead who is searching for traps spots the tripwire with a successful DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Once spotted, it can easily be avoided or disarmed.

effect: The walls of the maze come crashing down. Every creature in the collapsing maze is hit by debris and must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one.
area: The entire maze in area X12
description: A tripwire rigged halfway through the maze in Ahmaergo's quarters causes the walls of the maze to collapse when triggered.

name: Beholder Wall Carving Trap
trigger: Pushing either button (the eye of a wizard carving) or using an object or spell to do so

detection.detail: Any character who studies the carvings on the west wall and succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check notices that each wizard's eye is a button that can be pushed.

disarm.detail: A character can forcibly reset a button by making a successful DC 20 Dexterity check using thieves' tools. Once a button is pushed, it locks in place for 1 hour and can't be pushed again until that time elapses.

effect: The beholder carving on the wall discharges a green ray that the character can dodge with a successful DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. If the ray hits, the character appears to be disintegrated but is actually teleported to area X34a or X34b, depending on which button was pushed.
description: A wall carving of a beholder that fires a green teleportation ray when a hidden button is pushed.

name: Lockbox (Cult Regalia)
trigger: Attempting to open the lockbox without the proper key

detection.detail: The lockbox is hidden under a stack of quilts bearing images of flying devils.

disarm.detail: The box can be unlocked with either Wilifort's or Tissina's golden key, or by a character who succeeds on a DC 14 Dexterity check using thieves' tools. It can also be pried open with a successful DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check.

effect: The lockbox contains cult regalia (see "Cult of Asmodeus," page 115).
description: A gold-embellished lockbox hidden under a stack of quilts bearing images of flying devils, containing cult regalia.

name: Golden Lockbox Poison Gas Trap
trigger: Opening the lockbox by any means other than a golden key

detection.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

disarm.detail: This trap can't be disarmed.

effect: Poison gas sprays out from holes in the underside of the lid, filling a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on the box. The gas dissipates quickly.
description: A poison gas trap on a golden lockbox hidden under the bed in the master bedroom of the Cassalanter villa.

name: Cold Trap
trigger: If a creature enters the vault without first saying "Gold is my shield," an intense blast of magical cold fills the room.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals the secret to disabling the trap: a tiny magical glyph is inscribed in the middle of the ceiling.

disarm.detail: If this glyph is dispelled with a successful casting of dispel magic (DC 16), the trap ceases to function.

effect: All creatures in the vault at that time must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw, taking 36 (8d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A magical cold trap in the false vault that triggers when a creature enters without speaking the passphrase.

name: Collapsing Floor
trigger: Any Medium or larger creature that steps onto a 5-foot-square marked C on the map

detection.detail: The balcony floors have weakened with age.

effect: The floor crumbles and falls away, leaving a gaping hole. On a failed save, the creature falls 20 feet and lands prone on the floor below (area A7) amid stone debris. On a success, the creature avoids the fall by leaping to an adjacent, unoccupied space. The sound of the collapsing floor can be heard throughout the temple.
description: The balcony floors have weakened with age. Any Medium or larger creature that steps onto a 5-foot-square marked C on the map must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw as the floor crumbles and falls away, leaving a gaping hole.

name: Wooden Trunk Spider Swarm Trap
trigger: Lifting the lid of the wooden trunk

detection.detail: No detection check specified; trap triggers when trunk is opened.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: Panels in the front and sides open, releasing a swarm of mechanical spiders that attacks anyone other than Jarlaxle.
description: A wooden trunk that releases a swarm of mechanical spiders when opened.

name: Floor Clamps
trigger: Pulling a lever is an action that causes both clamps to release the floor, which is then magically driven upward into the ceiling.

detection.detail: The floor creaks and tilts slightly when stepped on, and it can be seen to be detached from the walls. Two oversized iron clamps on opposite sides of the room hold the floor in place. Each of these rusty mechanisms is attached to an iron lever.

effect: Creatures standing on the floor are knocked prone and must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw as they slam into the ceiling, taking 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The floor then settles a few feet below the ceiling, cutting off access to the stairs down to area K15 but leaving characters free to climb up the collapsed staircase to area K17. After 10 minutes, the floor descends to its normal level and the clamps lock it down again.
description: A magical clamped floor built as a precaution in case one of the experiments went berserk.

name: Golem Trap
trigger: The golem stands on a pressure plate. When it steps off the plate to attack someone out of its reach, the weight on the plate is lifted, causing poison gas to erupt from the holes in the walls.

detection.detail: Any character who inspects the hall for traps and succeeds on a DC 17 Wisdom (Perception) check notices 1-inch-diameter holes drilled into the walls at ankle height, set at regular intervals along the length of the passage.

effect: When the trap triggers, each creature in the hall must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The gas lingers for 1 minute unless dispersed with a gust of wind spell or similar magic.
description: A pressure plate trap that releases poison gas from holes in the walls when the flesh golem steps off it.

name: Poison Gas Trap
trigger: Opening the door or entering the hall triggers the trap
effect: Each creature in the hall must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The gas lingers for 1 minute unless dispersed with a gust of wind spell or similar magic. While the gas persists, a creature in the hall must repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns. The golem is immune to the poison gas.
description: A trap that releases poison gas in the hall.

name: Arcane Rune
trigger: The first time damage is dealt to the rune

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar magic reveals a powerful aura of conjuration magic around the rune. A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check confirms that this rune sustains the force field around Kolat Towers, and that the rune can be destroyed.

disarm.detail: The rune can't be dispelled normally, but each successful dispel magic cast on it (DC 19) deals 16 (3d10) force damage to it.

effect: The first time damage is dealt to the rune, a red slaad magically springs forth from it and attacks all creatures in the hallway. When the rune is destroyed, the force field around Kolat Towers disappears.
description: An elaborate rune inscribed on the back wall that sustains the force field around Kolat Towers. It has AC 10, 22 hit points, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

name: Snare
trigger: A character who fails to notice the trap triggers the snare.

detection.detail: If the characters are searching for traps, the character in the lead spots the trap automatically if his or her passive Wisdom (Perception) score is 12 or higher. Otherwise, the character must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice the trap.

disarm.detail: The character is restrained until 1 or more slashing damage is dealt to the snare's cord.

effect: The character is suspended upside down 10 feet above the ground. The character is restrained until 1 or more slashing damage is dealt to the snare's cord. A character who isn't carefully lowered down takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
description: A hidden snare on the goblin trail that suspends a character upside down.

name: Pit
trigger: The pit triggers when a creature moves across it.

detection.detail: The character in the lead spots the hidden pit automatically if his or her passive Wisdom (Perception) score is 15 or higher. Otherwise, the character must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to spot the hidden pit.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: The lead character must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall in, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage. The pit's walls are not steep, so no ability check is required to scramble out.
description: A camouflaged pit on the goblin trail.

name: Fragile Ledge
trigger: Any weight in excess of 100 pounds on the ledge between the two escarpments

detection.detail: Not explicitly stated; the ledge is described as fragile.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; it is a natural hazard.

effect: The whole mass loosens and tumbles down to the east. Any creature on the ledge when it falls must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. The creature also falls prone on a failed save.
area: The ledge between the two escarpments in the western passage
description: A fragile ledge that collapses under excessive weight, sending creatures tumbling down.

name: Flood!
trigger: The goblins in area 7 are signaled by the lookout in area 5 and knock away the supports, releasing a surge of water.

detection.detail: Not explicitly stated; the flood is a sudden event.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; it is a triggered trap.

effect: A water surge pours from area 7 down to area 1. Any creature within 10 feet of the disused passage at area 4 or the steps leading up to area 3 can attempt a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw to avoid being swept away. A creature that fails to get out of the way can attempt a DC 15 Strength saving throw to hold on. On a failed save, the character is knocked prone and washed down to area 1, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage along the way.
area: The main passage from area 7 down to area 1, specifically within 10 feet of the disused passage at area 4 or the steps leading up to area 3.
description: A trap that releases a surge of water down the main passage of the lair.

name: Hidden Pit Trap
trigger: The tiles and timbers collapse under 100 or more pounds of weight.

detection.detail: A character searching the hall for traps can spot the covered pit with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. A successful check also reveals narrow ledges on the north and south sides of the pit.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described in the source text.

effect: A creature that triggers the trap or fails the Dexterity check to skirt around the edge of the pit must attempt a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw to catch the edge. On a failed save, the creature falls 20 feet to the dirt floor of the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing prone.
area: The pit trap is in the middle of the hallway, hidden under a false floor consisting of loose stone tiles laid atop breakaway timbers. The pit is 20 feet deep.
description: A hidden pit trap in a hallway, covered by a false floor that collapses under 100 or more pounds of weight.

name: Collapsing Bridge
trigger: A creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across the south bridge.

detection.detail: A character next to the bridge can discern that the construction is faulty with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

disarm.method: Any creature can use an action to dislodge one end of either bridge, dropping it into the crevasse.
disarm.detail: Any creature can use an action to dislodge one end of either bridge, dropping it into the crevasse.

effect: The south bridge collapses when a creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across it, dropping the creature into the crevasse.
area: The south wooden bridge spanning the crevasse.
description: The south bridge is rigged to collapse when a creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across it.

name: Crevasse
trigger: A creature falls into the crevasse.

detection.detail: The crevasse is an open fissure, 5 to 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep, easily visible.

disarm.detail: The crevasse cannot be disarmed.

effect: A creature that falls into the crevasse takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and lands prone in a jumble of rubble that is difficult terrain. The bottom of the crevasse feels unnaturally cold. When viewed with a detect magic spell, the area emanates a faint necromantic aura. The magic causes all organic matter in the crevasse to age and decompose at half the normal rate.
area: A steep-sided fissure 5 to 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep.
description: A steep-sided fissure in the cavern floor that damages and knocks prone creatures that fall in, and magically ages organic matter at half the normal rate.

name: Cave-In Trap
trigger: Any creature that walks over or through the rubble without avoiding the tripwire triggers a cave-in of wooden beams and heavy stones.

detection.detail: Spotting the tripwire requires a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of at least 20, or a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check if characters are actively searching for traps in the area.

disarm.detail: Once spotted, the tripwire is easily avoided and disarmed (no ability check required).

effect: A cave-in of wooden beams and heavy stones. Any creature in the area when the trap triggers must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage from the falling rubble (half as much damage on a successful save). The noise of the collapse puts the monsters in areas 3, 7, 8, and 9 on alert.
area: The area of the collapse is marked on the map.
description: A copper tripwire connected to linchpins hidden in the ruined ceiling, concealed by dusty plaster and rubble in front of the door leading to area 8.

name: Trap in Area 2
trigger: Unknown (referenced but not detailed in this text)
effect: Unknown (referenced but not detailed in this text)
description: A trap located in area 2 of the Cragmaw Castle. Goblins avoid the north door of the banquet hall because of this trap.

name: Poison Gas
trigger: Whenever a creature attempts to cross the cavern, the carpets of fungi that cover most of the floor release poisonous gas into the air.

detection.detail: The glowing fungi allow creatures to see the entire cavern without the aid of darkvision or a light source.

effect: Each creature in the cavern must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 poison damage and be poisoned for 10 minutes. The gas disperses after 1 minute, but until then, any living creature that ends its turn in the cavern must repeat the saving throw.
description: A cavern covered in glowing fungi that release poisonous gas when creatures attempt to cross.

name: Ceiling Collapse
trigger: Removing either jewel eye from the statue

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals a strong aura of abjuration magic surrounding the statue.

effect: The pillars that line the walls crack, triggering a ceiling collapse. Each creature in the room must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 bludgeoning damage from falling rubble and falling prone on a failure, or taking only half the damage on a success.
description: A trap that causes the ceiling to collapse when either jewel eye is removed from a statue.

name: Boulder Ambush
trigger: Characters walk into the trap set by the rearguard cultists positioned in the rocks above.

detection.detail: If characters haven't been warned about the rearguard, someone spots a face peering down from above with a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check, but not until the characters are within 20 yards. If stragglers described the likely ambush spot to characters, it can be recognized from 200 yards away with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check. If stragglers mentioned the rearguard but didn't describe the spot, it is recognized as a good spot for an ambush from 100 yards away with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. If players state that they're watching for potential ambush spots, give them advantage when making these checks.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described in the source text.

effect: The cultists tumble boulders onto the characters. The boulder attack constitutes the cultists' surprise round. After that, they use ranged attacks until they are out of ammunition or the heroes force them into melee. Because they are positioned in the rocks above the characters, the cultists have three-quarters cover against attacks from below (+5 bonus to AC). To reach the foes, characters must scramble up the rocks. The distance is only 10 to 15 feet and no ability check is required, but the rocks are difficult terrain.
area: Characters walking into the trap along the trail through the gap between two outcrops.
description: A rearguard of cultists hidden in rocks 12 to 15 feet above ground level ambushes intruders by tumbling boulders onto them.

name: Trapped Stairs (Area 3)
trigger: The stairs are constructed so that the lowest steps collapse into a ramp that dumps a character right at the base of the violet fungi. Roll any die as each character descends the steps; on an odd roll, the character triggers the trap.

detection.detail: A character who is actively looking for a trap on the stairs can find the trapped step with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The kobolds and guards know where to avoid stepping, of course.

effect: The lowest steps collapse into a ramp that dumps a character right at the base of the violet fungi.
description: The stairs down to area 3 are trapped so that the lowest steps collapse into a ramp that dumps a character right at the base of the violet fungi.

name: Trapped Curtain (Area 6)
trigger: The curtain across the entrance to this cavern is trapped.

detection.detail: See 'Trapped Curtain' below for details.

effect: See 'Trapped Curtain' below for details.
area: The curtain across the entrance to this cavern
description: The curtain across the entrance to this cavern is trapped.

name: Trapped Curtain
trigger: Anyone who brushes through the curtain

detection.detail: A careful inspection of the leather strips coupled with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check finds barbs; they can't be noticed otherwise.

disarm.detail: When kobolds use this stairway, they bring the ruined spear that's kept in area 4. With it, they sweep the leather strips to the left side of the corridor and wedge the end of the spear shaft into an angled socket in the floor just inside area 6. This holds the leather strips safely out of the way while they move in and out of the chamber.

effect: Hidden in the patches of fur still clinging to the leather strips of the curtain are hundreds of metal barbs about the size of large fishhooks. The barbs are coated with poison. Anyone who brushes through the curtain must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 5 (1d10) poison damage, and the target's hit point maximum is reduced by 5. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest.
area: The curtain extends from wall to wall.
description: A curtain of leather strips hides metal barbs coated with poison.

name: Spike Trap
trigger: Each time a character moves between areas 4 and 7, roll a d10. On a roll of 1 or 2, that character's foot has gone through the trap.

detection.detail: It can be spotted incidentally with a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, or automatically by someone who is systematically tapping the floor ahead with a pole or other tool.

effect: A portion of the floor between areas 4 and 7 has been replaced with a sheet of parchment cleverly painted to resemble the surrounding stone. Beneath the parchment sheet is a shallow pit (about 2 feet deep) lined with poisoned spikes. The character takes 1d4 piercing damage from the spikes and must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw against poison. On a failed save, the character is affected as by a confusion spell for one minute (10 rounds). On a successful save, the character is affected as by a confusion spell for 1 round. The effect is not magical.
area: A portion of the floor between areas 4 and 7
description: A hidden pit lined with poisoned spikes.

name: Collapsing Trap
trigger: As each character enters the staircase, roll any die. On an odd roll, the character steps in the wrong spot and triggers the trap.

detection.detail: A character who is actively looking for a trap on the stairs can find the trapped step with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check. The collapsible ceiling is spotted incidentally with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

effect: The top step is rigged to drop a portion of the ceiling in area 7. The ceiling collapses above the next character in line (the one behind the character who triggered the trap). That character takes 4d4 bludgeoning damage from falling rocks; the damage is halved if the character makes a successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. Every character within 5 feet takes 2d4 bludgeoning damage, or half that with a successful saving throw.
area: The top step and the ceiling above area 7
description: A rigged step that causes a portion of the ceiling to collapse.

name: Acid Trap
trigger: The trap has two triggers. The first is under the chest in the northwest corner. If the chest is moved, the trap goes off. The second is in the chest. If it is forced open, or if the lock is inexpertly picked (a Dexterity result of 14 or less), the trap goes off.

detection.detail: A detailed search coupled with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check spots that many of the black dragon carvings have holes in their mouths.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: You hear a snap from beneath the chest, followed by a hissing sound like dozens of angry snakes— or like liquid moving through open tubes. A moment later, liquid sprays out from dozens of tiny holes in the walls and ceiling. Wherever it splashes onto the floor, the moisture on the stone bubbles and smokes. Within moments, the chamber is filled with acidic mist. Everyone in the chamber must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 acid damage from the acid sprayed onto them (half as much damage on a successful saving throw). The real danger from the acid is not to the characters’ skin, however, but to their lungs. Everyone must also succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 extra acid damage. Players who declare immediately that their characters are covering their faces and getting out of the chamber as quickly as possible, and are trying to not inhale the vapor, have advantage on their Constitution saving throws.
description: A trap that sprays acidic mist from holes in the dragons’ mouths, triggered by moving the chest or forcing it open.

name: Chute Trap
trigger: Someone steps on the chute without knowing it's there

detection.detail: The slight depression it causes in the rug can be noticed with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check.

effect: The character must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. Success means the character hops off the rug before it collapses through the hole, or grabs the top of ladder as he or she falls; failure means the character plunges 30 feet down the chute into area 9, taking 3d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
description: An open chute covered by rugs that drops 30 feet down to area 9.

name: Camouflaged Trapdoor
trigger: A creature steps on or interacts with the camouflaged trapdoor in the floor of the strong room.

detection.detail: It can be found with a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check.

effect: The trapdoor opens, revealing a dripping, slimy tunnel that runs 500 yards into a dense stand of trees and brush at the edge of the Mere of Dead Men.
area: Floor of the strong room (area 4) at the Carnath Roadhouse.
description: A camouflaged trapdoor in the floor of the strong room connects to a tunnel used by lizardfolk to smuggle contraband into the Mere of Dead Men.

name: Quicksand
trigger: A creature steps into the quicksand

detection.detail: Not specified in the source text

disarm.detail: Cannot be disarmed; escape via DC 15 Strength check or rescue via DC 15 Strength check

effect: A creature that steps into the quicksand must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw or sink into the quicksand and be restrained. On its turn, as part of its movement, the trapped creature can escape by making a DC 15 Strength check. Another creature can attempt to pull the restrained creature out of the quicksand as an action but must succeed on a DC 15 Strength check to do so. As in a movie, the trapped creature is always more than 5 feet from the edge of the quicksand, so rescuers can't just grab the character; they must find a vine, a rope, or a pole and toss it to where the trapped character can reach it.
area: The quicksand patch; trapped creature is always more than 5 feet from the edge
description: A patch of quicksand in the Mere of Dead Men that restrains creatures who step into it.

name: Magical Ward on Spellbook Box
trigger: Opening the box without the key, or failing a Dexterity check to pick the lock by 5 or more (roll less than 20)

detection.detail: No detection method specified; the trap is triggered by tampering with the lock.

disarm.method: Opening the box with the key
disarm.detail: Opening the box with the key disarms the trap automatically; Jos carries the key on a string around his neck.

effect: A magical ward with the same effect as a Melf's acid arrow spell launches at the character who opened the box.
damage: 4d6 acid damage immediately plus another 4d6 acid damage at the end of the character's next turn
area: The character who opened the box
description: A locked box of silver-inlaid redwood containing Azbara Jos's traveling spellbook is protected by a magical ward that triggers if the lock is tampered with.

name: Wardrobe Acid Trap
trigger: Opening the wardrobe without disarming the trap or failing the Dexterity check to disarm it

detection.detail: The trap can be detected with a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: Dexterity (thieves' tools) or Rezmir's insignia of claws
disarm.detail: Once spotted, the trap can be disarmed automatically by using Rezmir's insignia of claws or with a set of thieves' tools and a successful DC 20 Dexterity check.

effect: Vials of acid explode, causing 25 (7d6) acid damage to everyone in area 3N. Damage is halved with a successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw; the character who set off the trap has disadvantage on the saving throw. All Cult of the Dragon items in the wardrobe are ruined by acid, as are most of the furnishings and other objects in the room, including the dragon statuette described below.
description: A trapped wardrobe containing Rezmir's Cult of the Dragon regalia, rigged to explode with acid when opened improperly.

name: Slippery Steps
trigger: A character walks down the steps from area 3 to area 4.

detection.detail: The steps are visibly slippery due to mud slopping over the lip of stones.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified; characters can avoid the steps or proceed carefully.

effect: The character tumbles into area 4, taking 1d4 bludgeoning damage and making a lot of noise.
area: The steps descending 10 feet from area 3 to area 4.
description: Muddy steps that cause characters to slip and fall.

name: Pharblex's Chest Trap
trigger: If the chest is moved or if the hasp is not opened properly, six clay pots drop from concealed niches in the ceiling.

detection.detail: The trap can be spotted by someone who inspects the chest or the ceiling and succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Not specified in the source text.

effect: Six clay pots drop from concealed niches in the ceiling. Roll a d6 to determine how many pots shatter on the floor. The pots contain fine powder coated with hallucinogenic frog poison. Every creature in the chamber that is neither a frog nor a bullywug must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 11 + the number of pots that broke. A creature that succeeds on the save is unaffected. A creature that fails the saving throw succumbs to the hallucination that all other creatures in the chamber have been transformed into nightmarish, frog-like monstrosities. While affected, the creature cannot take reactions and must roll a die at the start of each of its turns. If the die result is odd, the creature must use its action and all of its available movement to move to area 6, enter the pool, and remain underwater. If the die result is even, the hallucinating creature attacks the nearest creature to it, treating it as hostile. The effect lasts for 10 minutes.
description: A trapped wooden chest in Pharblex's Sanctum that releases hallucinogenic poison pots when moved or improperly opened.

name: Needle Trap
trigger: A creature triggers the needle trap.

detection.detail: A needle can be found with a successful DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

disarm.detail: Can be disarmed with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check.

effect: A creature triggering the needle trap or failing the Dexterity check by 5 or more is injected with wyvern poison and must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 24 (7d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
description: A needle trap that injects wyvern poison into a creature that triggers it or fails to disarm it.

name: Weakened Walkway
trigger: When a character reaches the bend in the walkway, have the player roll any die. If an odd number is rolled, a portion of the wall crumbles.

detection.detail: A visual inspection from either doorway indicates that the walkway looks safe enough—aside from being icy, narrow, and adjacent to an apparently bottomless pit. The walkway that crosses the east and north sides of the chamber is, in fact, safe, and characters can walk along it without difficulty. The walkway that crosses the west and south walls is weakened and dangerous.

effect: A portion of the wall crumbles, and any creature on the walkway must attempt a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is pushed off the walkway into the chute. The chute drops 60 feet to the top of the ice platform in area 16 in Arauthator's lair. A creature tipped into the chute slides as much as falls, taking only 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage when hitting bottom. The creature must then attempt a Dexterity saving throw or fall off the ice platform; see area 16 for more information. A creature that jumps into the chute on purpose takes half damage from the descent and has advantage on the saving throw to stay on the ice platform.
area: The walkway that crosses the west and south walls of the chamber.
description: A weakened and dangerous icy walkway around a pit in the chute chamber. When a character reaches the bend, a die roll determines if the wall crumbles, potentially pushing them into the chute.

name: The Gullet
trigger: When the first character passes through the narrowest point of the passage
effect: the entire area of the passage fills with a stinking cloud for 1 minute. Arauthator immediately becomes aware of intruders if the stinking cloud is triggered. The dragon does not set off the trap if it moves through the area.
area: the entire area of the passage
description: This narrow passage is rigged with a magic trap that fills the area with a stinking cloud.

name: The Throat
trigger: When the first character moves through the narrowest point of the passage
effect: a slow spell is triggered, targeting every creature in the area. Creatures affected by the spell suffer its effects for 1 minute. Arauthator immediately becomes aware of intruders if the slow spell is triggered. The dragon does not set off the trap if it moves through the area.
description: This narrow passage is rigged with a magic trap that triggers a slow spell.

name: Statue Trap
trigger: When the first adventurer passes the halfway point of the room, the sound of grinding stone announces the statues turning their cowled heads to follow the characters' movements.

detection.detail: The sound of grinding stone announces the statues turning their cowled heads to follow the characters' movements.

effect: The characters must not look into the darkness in the statues' hoods. Any character who does must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw.
area: The room with six statues of cowled wizards
description: Six statues of cowled wizards lean on staffs, their faces obscured by deep hoods. When characters pass the halfway point, the statues turn their heads to follow their movements. Looking into the darkness in the hoods triggers a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw.

name: Door Hazard
trigger: Pulling on either door unleashes enough force to break the hinges and send the doors and a wall of rubble crashing into the room.

detection.detail: The doors bulge out noticeably from their frame, pushed out by the weight of stone where the ceiling of the corridor between area 4 and area 12 has collapsed.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

effect: Any creature within 10 feet of the doors must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw to jump out of the way. On a failure, the creature takes 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage, or half damage on a successful save. The fall of rubble leaves the hallway filled with stone and impassable.
area: Any creature within 10 feet of the doors.
description: A hazard where pulling on the doors causes them and a wall of rubble to crash into the room.

name: Bone Boulder Trap
trigger: A mechanical plate installed in the floor triggers a rolling boulder trap.

detection.detail: A successful DC 22 Wisdom (Perception) check by one of the characters in the first rank of the marching order is required to notice this trigger without activating the pressure plate.

effect: If the plate is activated, the circular mosaic pattern that appears as the sun on the floor in area 4 slides back and a 7-foot-diameter sphere made of hundreds of skeletal bodies rises magically from the floor. This bone boulder tilts toward area 6 and rolls down the sloping hallway before crashing against the wall in area 7. As it rolls through, the bone boulder crushes and slashes at any creature in area 6, dealing 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and 18 (4d8) slashing damage, or half damage with a successful DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. Any creature that fails this first save is grabbed by skeletal hands and pulled into the sphere, which continues to roll over any other creatures in the hallway. A creature trapped in the bone boulder can attempt a DC 17 Strength or Dexterity check to break free before the boulder slams into the wall in area 7. Any creature that fails to escape is inside the boulder when it hits, and is caught in an explosion of bones and stone, taking 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and 14 (4d6) slashing damage.
damage: 18 (4d8) bludgeoning and 18 (4d8) slashing, plus 14 (4d6) bludgeoning and 14 (4d6) slashing if trapped
description: A rolling boulder trap made of skeletal bodies that crushes and slashes creatures in its path.

name: Dart Trap
trigger: When any creature steps on the pressure plate

detection.detail: revealed by a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check

effect: darts shoot out from the walls along the length of the hallway, targeting all creatures in the area: +8 to hit, 3 (1d6) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage and be paralyzed for 1 minute.
description: A pressure plate 10 feet before the archway triggers darts from the walls along the hallway.

name: Magic Glyph of Warding (Slow)
trigger: Opening the locked wooden chest without the proper key or failing to disarm the lock

detection.detail: A character can find the glyph with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check

disarm.detail: Opening the lock requires thieves' tools and a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. A failed check sets off the trap.

effect: A slow spell affects all creatures in the area except elementals. Creatures affected can attempt the saving throw again at the end of each of their turns. Otherwise, the effect ends after 1 minute.
area: All creatures in the area except elementals
description: A magic glyph of warding protects a locked chest in area 15. Failing to pick the lock triggers a slow spell.

name: Meteor Swarm Trap
trigger: Moving along the Cosmic Hallway (area 17)

detection.detail: No detection method specified; the swarm of meteors shoots past at an opportune moment

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified

effect: A swarm of tiny meteors shoots past, threatening to knock creatures off the walkway. All creatures on the path must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw to dodge the meteors. On a failed save, a creature is struck, takes 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage, and is knocked off the walkway. A creature knocked off the walkway appears to fall into infinite space. Unless the creature can fly or teleport back to the walkway, it quickly vanishes from sight. Roll 1d4 + 17; the number rolled is the number of the room where the character materializes and crashes to the floor on the following round, taking 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage from the fall.
damage: 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage, plus 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage from the fall
area: All creatures on the path in area 17
description: A hazard in the Cosmic Hallway where a swarm of tiny meteors threatens to knock creatures off the walkway into infinite space.

name: Paper Whirlwind Swarms
trigger: Opening either secret door in area 18 (Study) by anyone other than Xonthal

detection.detail: The secret doors can be found with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, but the trap itself is triggered by opening the door

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified; the swarms remain on guard for 30 minutes then collapse

effect: Thousands of sheets of heavy paper fly into the air in a great whirlwind, slashing at any creature in the area. One distinct storm of paper forms around each character on the first round. Every round after that, two more cyclones form, to a maximum of three per character. Treat these paper whirlwinds as swarms of ravens, but they are constructs instead of beasts, and they have vulnerability to fire. When the paper swarms form, they remain on guard in the study for 30 minutes, then collapse to piles of paper once more. They won't pursue characters into the hallway, but will chase them into the two adjoining rooms.
area: The study (area 18) and the two adjoining rooms
description: A magical trap in the Study that animates paper into swarms of ravens (constructs with vulnerability to fire) when the secret doors are opened by anyone but Xonthal.

name: Doomsand
trigger: A creature starts its turn in doomsand

detection.detail: Similar in most ways to standard quicksand, doomsand follows the same rules for sinking and escaping.

disarm.detail: Follows the same rules for sinking and escaping as standard quicksand.

effect: A creature that starts its turn in doomsand must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or become despondent (see Shadow Corruption below). When the creature finishes a long rest, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success.
area: Marshes and swamps, or in deserts as fine dust
description: Similar in most ways to standard quicksand, doomsand follows the same rules for sinking and escaping. This ashen-gray slurry is infused with the nature of shadow, and it drains the resolve from those in its grasp.

name: Hungry Gloom
trigger: Entering an area of hungry gloom

detection.detail: An area of hungry gloom appears particularly dark and grim, swallowing light.

effect: An area of light that overlaps hungry gloom has its illumination reduced by one step (bright light becomes dim, dim light becomes darkness). Darkvision can't improve the ambient light conditions in the area. Shadow-touched creatures (see Shadow Corruption below) can see in hungry gloom as if it were bright light.
area: Some areas of the Shadow Realm—or places in the mortal world where the barrier to the Shadow Realm is thin
description: Some areas of the Shadow Realm—or places in the mortal world where the barrier to the Shadow Realm is thin—develop hungry gloom. An area of hungry gloom appears particularly dark and grim, swallowing light.

name: Leaden Clouds
trigger: Being beneath a leaden cloud of sorrow

detection.detail: These dark, heavy clouds oppress the spirit of those beneath them, serving as a sort of psychic weight.

disarm.detail: Certain items, such as emerald goblets (see Chapter 10), and spells, such as aid, calm emotions, enthrall, and lesser restoration, and even a barbarian's Rage ability negate the effects of leaden clouds.

effect: Creatures under a leaden cloud of sorrow must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom or Charisma saving throw to make an attack, cast a spell, or move at more than a standard walking pace (though they can still defend themselves normally).
area: Beneath a leaden cloud of sorrow
description: These dark, heavy clouds oppress the spirit of those beneath them, serving as a sort of psychic weight.

name: Radiant Well
trigger: A creature enters a radiant well

detection.detail: This form of well resembles a beacon of light at the surface, though it swallows up anything thrown into it. A radiant well is a planar link to one of the celestial planes, and it sheds searing, bright daylight in a 60-foot radius around itself and up into the clouds.

effect: Any creature entering a radiant well falls for 1 round and then is ejected upward at relatively high speed from another well within 2d20 miles (for evil creatures, this increases to 1d100 miles). The force of being ejected from the well propels a Small or smaller creature up about 30 feet before falling to the ground beside the well (potentially taking normal falling damage). Medium and Large creatures are pushed up about 15 feet, and Huge or larger creatures simply land at the edge of the well. Particularly large or active radiant wells sometimes inflict radiant damage on evil-aligned creatures.
area: 60-foot radius of bright daylight around the well
description: This form of well resembles a beacon of light at the surface, though it swallows up anything thrown into it. A radiant well is a planar link to one of the celestial planes, and it sheds searing, bright daylight in a 60-foot radius around itself and up into the clouds.

name: Shadow Mire
trigger: A creature steps into shadow mire

detection.detail: This resembles dark water and is indistinguishable from water at night—leaves and reeds may float on it, and it reflects moonlight normally.

effect: Stepping into shadow mire generates an immediate, oversized wave that radiates from the creature entering the mire, knocking down all in its path. Any creatures within 30 feet, which are smaller than the creature stepping into the mire, must succeed on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) saving throw or be knocked prone by the wave. The creature in the center of the mire will be covered by the shadow mire as it rolls back to its point.
area: 30 feet around the creature stepping into the mire
description: Usually found along the shores of ponds, lakes, and streams, shadow mire is a concentration of pure shadow matter that has eaten away the soil, roots, and plants of a place and replaced them with a thin layer of viscous purple-black gloop.

name: Whispering Room
trigger: A creature takes a long rest in this room

detection.detail: The haunting is not hidden; its effects are experienced directly by anyone resting in the room.

disarm.detail: To end the haunting and bring rest to the ghost, Loris's murderer, Hiernanda Kitza (LE human archmage), now a powerful magic user, must spend a full night in the room—this may result in her death or a transfer of the whisper-curse, the constant sound of accusing whispers surrounding Kitza.

effect: A creature that takes a long rest in this room is wracked by vivid dreams, which rapidly alternate from a warm embrace and the sound of whispered endearments to skeletal hands wrapped around the dreamer's throat and the sound of hissed curses. At the end of the long rest, the creature gains no benefit from the rest, takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage, and gains one level of exhaustion. A successful DC 20 Wisdom saving throw avoids the psychic damage but not the other effects.
description: The inn's most opulent room, called the Whispering Room by the staff, is haunted by the spirit of Loris Treik, a maiden who was seduced by Gunrik Stoll and murdered in the room by Stoll's jealous human mistress, Hiernanda Kitza. Loris's ghost rarely appears in the room, preferring to haunt the dreams of those who sleep in it.

name: Roachling Pit
trigger: A creature approaches or rests near the water at the bottom of the pit; the slippery slope makes it difficult to leave, and creatures that stay near the water overnight or for a long rest slowly sink with the stones and the pool of water.

detection.detail: The pit appears as a gentle hollow or dip in the landscape with an enticing body of water at the bottom surrounded by reeds or trees, or as a set of stones or a small mesa with a pure water spring. No specific detection DC is given.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is provided.

effect: The gentle slope around the water is often quite slippery, making it difficult to leave the area around the water. Creatures must make a strong effort to climb back up the slope. Creatures that stay near the water overnight or for a long rest slowly sink with the stones and the pool of water, and on waking, may find themselves 30 or 40 feet below the level of the surroundings. The walls of the pit are commonly pockmarked with niches, tunnels, and small dwelling spaces, often inhabited.
area: A gentle hollow or dip in the landscape with a body of water at the bottom, or a set of stones or small mesa with a pure water spring.
description: A roachling pit is an entirely bizarre form of terrain made by congealing, spinning, and reforming raw shadow into demonic termite mounds or hollow dunes and curved pits, usually found on the plains with an enticing body of pure rainwater at the bottom.
